maxWords: How many words of the title are allowed to change the result.
Only the first this many words are scored against the patterns, and only those words enter the seed. The title is not copied into the instruction.
Set it to 0 and every title falls back to a generic pattern. The seed, when you pass one, still counts.
minScore: How strong a match has to be before a pattern can win.
A pattern scores above this, or it is ignored. If none do, a pattern with no triggers is used instead. That is the fallback for a title that has been rewritten past recognition.
The default is 0, so any overlap with a trigger is enough to leave the fallback.
patternSpread: How close to the best score another pattern must be to stay in the running.
1 means only the top score can win. 0.2, the default, lets a near miss share the win, with the stronger score winning more often. The seed makes the pick.
Lower it and more patterns are allowed to answer the same title.
sharedFactor: The chance, from 0 to 1, of borrowing a sentence shape from the shared templates.
The matched pattern still supplies the manner, the verb, the object, and the voice. Only the arrangement of those gaps changes.
0 keeps every instruction on the pattern's own templates.
quirks: Turns quirks mode on or off.
Off, each property is picked from its plain list. On, there is a quirk-factor chance that the quirky list is added to that pool before the pick.
The checkbox on the tester overrides this for that one run.
quirkFactor: When quirks mode is on, the chance, from 0 to 1, of a quirky result instead of a plain one.

That chance adds the quirky manners, verbs, objects, voices, and templates to the plain pools. At 1, the quirky rows are always added. At 0, quirks mode can be on and every instruction still stays plain.
It does nothing while quirks mode is off. The factor slider on the tester overrides this for that one run.
manners: The adverbs a plain instruction can use, in {manner}.
The seed picks one entry. It never invents a word that is not here. Order matters: the same input and seed always lands on the same place in the list.
Add a word and it becomes a possible choice. Remove one and plain instructions stop using it.
quirkyManners: Extra adverbs added to the {manner} pool when the quirky chance hits.
They are written the same way as the plain manners. A phrase is allowed.
With quirks off, or when the roll stays plain, these entries are not used.
verbs: The verbs a plain instruction can use, in {verb}.
Write the form the sentence needs. English defaults are bare verbs (combine, summarise), because the template supplies the rest.
Order matters, for the same reason it matters on every list.
quirkyVerbs: Extra verbs added to the {verb} pool when the quirky chance hits.
The English defaults are the playful ones, such as discombobulate and juxtapose.
With quirks off, or when the roll stays plain, these entries are not used.
objects: The thing the verb acts on, in {object}.
Each entry is a short noun phrase, such as the text or the sources. The template does not add the or a for you.
quirkyObjects: Extra objects added to the {object} pool when the quirky chance hits.
The English defaults include the themes and the digressions.
With quirks off, or when the roll stays plain, these entries are not used.
voices: Each row has an id, a name, and a phrase. The name is the persona the call returns. The phrase is what {voice} writes into the instruction, such as professionally or as a historian.
A row with an empty phrase is left out. Order matters. A pattern can bring its own actors, and those replace this list for that pattern.
quirkyVoices: Extra actors added to the voice pool when the quirky chance hits.

The English defaults include Douglas Adams, a beat poet, Hunter S. Thompson, and styles such as a hip hop song or an instruction manual. The name is still the persona, and the phrase is still what the instruction says.
With quirks off, or when the roll stays plain, these rows are not used. A pattern's own quirky actors are added as well when that pattern is chosen.
templates: The shared sentence shapes. A matched pattern uses its own templates most of the time.
Shared factor is the chance of using one of these shapes instead. The pattern's words are still filled in.
These shapes are also what a one-entry config uses when you pass templates and do not pass patterns.
quirkyTemplates: Extra shapes added to the template pool when the quirky chance hits.
Use them for a comma, a different order, or a frame you only want on a quirky roll.
With quirks off, or when the roll stays plain, these shapes are not used. The plain templates are still in the pool either way.
numbers: The strings slugger can write for {n}.
The English defaults are 2, 3, 5, two, three, five, and the quirky 42. A title that contains one of them selects a pattern marked Number. 101 is not in this list, so Lemurs 101 stays with essentials.
Add or remove a row to change which titles count as a list. A word is matched the same way as a trigger, so three and five still meet.
